title: Acyclicity on the closed projective line
statement:
In the setup of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselian-setup]: let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a strictly henselian local ring with residue field $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$, $X=\mathbf P^1_S=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};S)$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], $X_0=\mathbf P^1_s=X\times_Ss$ its closed fibre and $i:X_0\to X$ the closed immersion (the base change of $s\to S$). Let $r$ be a prime and $I$ an injective object of the category of sheaves of $\mathbf F_r$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and $I_0=i^{-1}I$ its inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Then

$$
 H^q(X_{0,\Et},I_0)=0\qquad(q>0),
$$

where $H^q$ is the etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] of the underlying abelian sheaf of $I_0$ (cohomology computed in abelian sheaves, as in the users and in the Lean statement).

(Remark. Stacks Lemma 0A5H assumes only that $A$ is henselian, and the proof below uses only that $(A,\mathfrak m)$ is a henselian pair; the hypothesis "strictly henselian" is kept because the setup [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselian-setup], the user [prop-weil-pbc-p1-strict-henselian-comparison] and the Lean declaration AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.subsingleton_H_projectiveLine_closedFibre_of_injective state it so. Stacks states the lemma for $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$-modules, $\ell$ prime, which is the present $\mathbf F_r$.)

proof.text: *The setting.* $A$ is strictly henselian, so $(A,\mathfrak m)$ is a henselian pair and $A$ is a henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]; $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m)=s$. The structure morphism $X=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};S)\to S$ is proper [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], hence separated and of finite type; since $S$ is affine, $X$ is separated, and its diagonal, a closed immersion, is affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] (a) and (c) with $S'=S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $X=D_+(T_0)_S\cup D_+(T_1)_S$ with both opens affine ($\cong\operatorname{Spec}A[U]$): $X$ is covered by $n+1=2$ affine opens. The closed fibre $X\times_SS_0$ is $X_0$ with inclusion $i$. Since $r\cdot I=0$, every local section of $I$ is killed by $r$, so $I$ is a torsion sheaf [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf]. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](2) the inverse image of a sheaf of $\mathbf F_r$-modules has as underlying abelian sheaf the abelian inverse image of the underlying abelian sheaf, and likewise for morphisms; direct images of sheaves of modules are computed sectionwise, so their underlying abelian sheaves are the abelian direct images. From now on all cohomology groups, pullback maps and maps $H^q(\varphi)$ are those of the underlying abelian sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial].

source.place: Stacks, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A5H (lemma-efface-cohomology-on-fibre-by-finite-cover), proof: 'Observe that X is a separated scheme which can be covered by 2 affine opens'

proof.text: *Degrees $q\ge2$.* Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-injective-restriction-acyclicity] to the henselian pair $(A,\mathfrak m)$, $Y=X$ (separated of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with affine diagonal, covered by $n+1=2$ affine opens, Step 1), $n=1$, $Y_0=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m)=X_0$, and the injective torsion sheaf of $\mathbf F_r$-modules $I$ (Stacks 0A51 takes $I$ injective in sheaves of $\mathcal A$-modules for a torsion sheaf of rings $\mathcal A$, here $\mathcal A=\underline{\mathbf F_r}$; the Lean form asks for an injective torsion sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules, $\Lambda=\mathbf F_r$): $H^q(X_0,I_0)=0$ for $q>1$. It remains to treat $q=1$.

source.place: Stacks, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A5H (lemma-efface-cohomology-on-fibre-by-finite-cover), proof: 'for q > 1 this follows from Gabber's affine variant of the proper base change theorem, see Lemma 0A51'

proof.text: *Representation of a class of $H^1$.* Let $\xi\in H^1(X_0,I_0)$. By [lemma-weil-pbc-h1-constructible-representation] (in the form of its Lean statement AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.exists_sum_eq_of_injective_projectiveLine) there are $m\ge0$ and, for $j=1,\dots,m$, a finite morphism of finite presentation $h_j:V_j\to X$, a finite $\mathbf F_r$-module $M_j$ with constant sheaf of $\mathbf F_r$-modules $\underline{M_j}$ on $V_{j,\Et}$, a morphism of sheaves of $\mathbf F_r$-modules $\psi_j:(h_j)_*\underline{M_j}\to I$ and a class $x_j\in H^1(X_0,i^{-1}(h_j)_*\underline{M_j})$, with $\xi=\sum_jH^1(i^{-1}\psi_j)(x_j)$. (This packages Stacks' reduction: $\xi$ comes from a constructible $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I$ by 03SA and 03Q5, $\mathcal F$ is enlarged into a finite sum of sheaves $f_*\underline M$ by 09Z7 using the injectivity of $\mathcal I$, and a direct sum is split into its summands.) By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-sheaf-underlying] the underlying abelian sheaf of $\underline{M_j}$ is the constant abelian sheaf with value the finite abelian group $M_j$; we write $\underline{M_j}$ for it as well. It suffices to show that each $x_j$ lies in the image of the pullback $i^*:H^1(X,(h_j)_*\underline{M_j})\to H^1(X_0,i^{-1}(h_j)_*\underline{M_j})$ (Steps 4-6), and then conclude (Step 7).

source.place: Stacks, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A5H (lemma-efface-cohomology-on-fibre-by-finite-cover), proof: second and third paragraphs, 'By Lemmas 03SA and 03Q5 we can find a map F → I ... By Lemma 09Z7 and the remarks above we may assume F is of the form f_*M'

proof.text:
*The closed fibre of $V_j$.* Fix $j$ and write $h=h_j:V\to X$, $M=M_j$. Let $V_0=V\times_XX_0$ with projections $i_V:V_0\to V$ and $h_0:V_0\to X_0$; this is a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with $h\circ i_V=i\circ h_0$, and $h_0$ is finite [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a). Pasting it with the cartesian square $X_0=X\times_Ss$, $V_0=V\times_S\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m)$ is the closed fibre of $V\to S$ (pasting of cartesian squares). Since $h$ is finite, the underived exchange morphism $\Ex^0:i^{-1}h_*\underline M\to h_{0*}i_V^{-1}\underline M$ [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] is an isomorphism [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange]; and $i_V^{-1}\underline M_V\cong\underline M_{V_0}$ canonically [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant]. The edge maps $e_h:H^1(X,h_*\underline M)\to H^1(V,\underline M)$ and $e_{h_0}:H^1(X_0,h_{0*}i_V^{-1}\underline M)\to H^1(V_0,i_V^{-1}\underline M)$ are bijective since $h,h_0$ are finite [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-cohomology] (Stacks: Leray spectral sequence 03QC and vanishing of higher direct images of finite morphisms 03QP). By [lem-weil-pbc-edge-map-base-change] for this square,
$$i_V^*\circ e_h=e_{h_0}\circ H^1(\Ex^0)\circ i^*:\ H^1(X,h_*\underline M)\to H^1(V_0,i_V^{-1}\underline M).$$

source.place: Stacks, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A5H (lemma-efface-cohomology-on-fibre-by-finite-cover), proof: 'Since formation of f_* commutes with any base change (Lemma 0959) ... By the Leray spectral sequence (Proposition 03QC) and vanishing of higher direct images (Proposition 03QP), we find H^1(X_0, f_*M|_{X_0}) = H^1(Y_0, M)'

proof.text: *Lifting over the proper $V$.* $V\to S$ is the composite of the finite $h$ and the proper $X\to S$ (Step 1), hence proper [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](c). So the hypotheses of [thm-weil-pbc-finite-etale-lifting] hold for the henselian pair $(A,\mathfrak m)$, $Y=V$ and $Y_0=V_0$ (Step 4), and [lemma-weil-pbc-h1-torsor-comparison] for the finite abelian group $M$ shows that restriction $H^1(V,\underline M)\to H^1(V_0,\underline M)$, i.e. $H^1(c)\circ i_V^*$ with $c:i_V^{-1}\underline M_V\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline M_{V_0}$ the isomorphism of [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant], is bijective. As $H^1(c)$ is bijective (functoriality of $H^1(-)$ for the isomorphism $c$, [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]), $i_V^*:H^1(V,\underline M)\to H^1(V_0,i_V^{-1}\underline M)$ is bijective. (Only the henselian property of $A$ is used here.)

source.place: Stacks, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A5H (lemma-efface-cohomology-on-fibre-by-finite-cover), proof: 'Since Y → Spec(A) is proper we can use Lemma 0A5G to see that H^1(Y_0, M) is equal to H^1(Y, M)'

proof.text: *Each $x_j$ lifts to $X$.* With the notation of Step 4, put $y=e_{h_0}(H^1(\Ex^0)(x_j))\in H^1(V_0,i_V^{-1}\underline M)$. By Step 5 there is $w\in H^1(V,\underline M)$ with $i_V^*w=y$, and by Step 4 there is $z_j\in H^1(X,h_*\underline M)$ with $e_h(z_j)=w$. Then by the identity of Step 4, $e_{h_0}H^1(\Ex^0)(i^*z_j)=i_V^*e_h(z_j)=y=e_{h_0}H^1(\Ex^0)(x_j)$, and since $e_{h_0}$ and $H^1(\Ex^0)$ are bijective (Step 4), $i^*z_j=x_j$.

source.place: Stacks, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A5H (lemma-efface-cohomology-on-fibre-by-finite-cover), proof: 'Thus we see that our cohomology class ζ lifts to a cohomology class ζ~ ∈ H^1(Y, M) = H^1(X, f_*M)'

proof.text: *Conclusion.* $I$ is an injective sheaf of $\mathbf F_r$-modules, so its underlying abelian sheaf has $H^1(X,I)=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-injective-module-abelian-acyclic] (with $R=\mathbf F_r$ and $U=X$). By the naturality clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] for $\psi_j$ and Step 6, $H^1(i^{-1}\psi_j)(x_j)=H^1(i^{-1}\psi_j)(i^*z_j)=i^*\bigl(H^1(\psi_j)(z_j)\bigr)=i^*(0)=0$ (this is the commutative square of Stacks). Hence $\xi=\sum_jH^1(i^{-1}\psi_j)(x_j)=0$, so $H^1(X_0,I_0)=0$; with Step 2, $H^q(X_0,I_0)=0$ for all $q>0$.

source.place: Stacks, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A5H (lemma-efface-cohomology-on-fibre-by-finite-cover), proof: 'However, ζ~ maps to zero in H^1(X, I) as I is injective and by commutativity of [the square] we conclude that the image ξ of ζ is zero as well'

split_report.summary: Rewrote the one-paragraph agent proof as seven steps following Stacks 0A5H (etale-cohomology.tex l.16164) and its proof: setting (P^1_A proper, separated, affine diagonal, two affine charts; I torsion; cohomology of underlying abelian sheaves), q>=2 by lemma-weil-pbc-injective-restriction-acyclicity with n=1 (hypotheses checked against 0A51 and its Lean), q=1 via the packaged representation lemma-weil-pbc-h1-constructible-representation (read in its Lean form: classes x_j of i^{-1}(h_j)_*M_j and maps psi_j into I), then for each j: finite exchange, constant-sheaf pullback, finite edge-map bijections (lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-cohomology, closed) and their compatibility with base change (lem-weil-pbc-edge-map-base-change, which the blueprint proof hid under 'the restriction square is commutative'), the H^1 torsor comparison over the proper V_j (hypotheses of thm-weil-pbc-finite-etale-lifting checked: V_j proper over the henselian pair (A,m) via lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence), H^1(X,I)=0 by lem-weil-pbc-injective-module-abelian-acyclic, naturality clause (3) of pullback. Statement made self-contained (prime r, injective in F_r-module sheaves, cohomology of the underlying abelian sheaf) with a remark that Stacks needs only A henselian. One new node (lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-sheaf-underlying, Mathlib leaf CategoryTheory.constantCommuteCompose). Tool uses outside the unit route: lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts (sk-thm-reduction), lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper (closed).
